predecessors.name: Kingdom of Israel
predecessors.text: the south of the united monarchy: Judah and Benjamin, after 'ten of the tribes rebelled against Rehoboam' c.

successors.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
successors.text: 'the fallen kingdom was annexed as a Babylonian province', Yehud, with Mizpah in Benjamin as its centre

ledger.x: c. 930: Judah splits from Israel. 'ten of the tribes rebelled against Rehoboam' and formed the northern Kingdom of Israel, leaving Rehoboam in Jerusalem.

c. 930: Israel and Judah at war. 'Israel and Judah warred throughout Rehoboam's 17-year reign'; Baasha later 'built a fortress at Ramah on the border, less than ten miles from Jerusalem' and Asa fortified Geba and Mizpah in Benjamin 'on his side of the border' (no years).

c. 911: end of the fighting, bridged to the end of Abijah's reign. The Abijah of Judah page (opened 2026-10-19): reign 'c. 913 – 911 BCE', a march north 'in the 18th year of King Jeroboam I', the 'Battle of Mount Zemaraim' and the capture of Jeshanah, Ephron…
800: Judah's western edge advances toward Lachish.
609 (bridged): the Assyrian overlordship ends with the empire.

605: the Egyptian overlordship ends at Carchemish: 'when the Egyptians were defeated by the Babylonians at Carchemish in 605 BCE, Jehoiakim changed allegiances to pay tribute to Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon'.

605: Judah pays tribute to Babylon (the sentence quoted above); after the deportation of 597 Zedekiah 'was made a tributary of Babylon'. neo-babylonian-empire /ledger/5 starts the vassalage at -597; this ledger follows the Kingdom of Judah…
586: the tribute ends with the fall of Jerusalem and the annexation of the land as the Babylonian province of Yehud (the loss below).

wars.name: Israel-Judah wars of Rehoboam
wars.outcome: No decisive result; the kingdoms stay separate; Egypt's Shishak took many Judean cities in Rehoboam's fifth year (Judah an Egyptian vassal, 10th century BCE).

wars.name: Sennacherib's campaign against Judah
wars.outcome: Hezekiah's refusal of tribute drew Sennacherib's invasion in 701; Judean fortified towns were destroyed or captured, Jerusalem was besieged but not taken, Hezekiah paid tribute, and the surrounding towns went to Assyrian vassal rulers in Ekron, Gaza and…

wars.name: Josiah at Megiddo
wars.outcome: Josiah tried to block Necho II's march to the Euphrates at Megiddo and was killed; On his return march in 608 Necho deposed Jehoahaz, installed Jehoiakim and levied a hundred talents of silver; Judah was an Egyptian vassal until 605 (vassal pair in the…

wars.name: Babylonian conquest of Judah
wars.outcome: Jehoiakim switched to Babylon after Carchemish (605); Jerusalem fell on 16 March 597; Zedekiah revolted and was besieged from 589; the city fell in 586 and Judah became the province of Yehud.

certainty.note: The page gives the frontier only in general terms (the Dead Sea, Jericho, Gezer, the Shephelah, Beersheba); no treaty or survey line.
